stories.headline: Nepal seeks to import power earlier from India after flood devastation, asks for approvals
stories.title: Nepal seeks to import power earlier from India after flood devastation, asks for approvals
stories.summary: While the Himalayan country usually imports electricity from India during the winter months, it has now asked that the required approvals for sending power be processed in September itself
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In the wake of the devastating flash flood that severely impacted Nepal’s power infrastructure, Kathmandu has asked India to give the requisite approvals for the transmission of electricity to Nepal earlier than usual, senior officials in the Union Power Ministry said on Saturday (August 29, 2026).
“Nepal has asked that India advance import approvals, starting from September this year, in view of the generation deficits caused by this disaster.
The concerned authorities are processing the requests,” an official said.
According to officials, India is willing to provide any additional power that Nepal may need.
Nepal usually imports electricity from India during the winter months, starting around October, as power generation is typically low in the Himalayan country during the freezing winter months.
Conversely, the country exports its excess hydropower to India during the summer.
According to official data, India imported 3,299 million units (MUs) of power from Nepal in fiscal year 2025-26 and exported 1,451 MUs to it.
Transmission of electricity across India’s borders requires mandatory clearances from the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), among others.
According to an internal assessment, Nepal’s electricity generation capacity has declined by about 550 megawatts because of the infrastructural damage induced by the flood.
Officials said that this resulted in the cross-border power flow to India reducing by approximately 400 MW from earlier peaks of 950 MW to 1,000 MW.
However, the officials assured that India was not foreseeing any requirement to make alternative arrangements to compensate for the shortfall.

“We do not foresee any requirement for exceptional emergency procurement or alternative arrangement to balance domestic demand,” an official said, adding, “India’s vast national grid capacity and robust generation reserve margins are capable of absorbing a temporary shortfall of 400 MW seamlessly without disrupting grid stability or retail supply."

stories.headline: Tharoor urges Centre to deploy full NDRF contingent for Nepal flood rescue
stories.title: Tharoor urges Centre to deploy full NDRF contingent for Nepal flood rescue
stories.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor urged the Centre to deploy a full NDRF contingent, heavy-lift helicopters and advanced search equipment in Nepal, where hundreds of Indians remain missing or stranded after devastating flash floods, stressing that rescue efforts must be intensified immediately
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: New Delhi: With several Indians still missing in the Nepal flash floods, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Saturday asked the Modi government for a full NDRF contingent and heavy-lift helicopters for rescue operations.
In his letter to External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, Tharoor urged the government to pull out all stops to rescue the stranded or those who may still be alive beneath the debris.

On Wednesday, an ice-rock avalanche following a glacial collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border sent a torrent of water, mud and debris downstream, wiping out towns and villages, damaging crucial infrastructure and washing away hydropower stations through central Nepal.
“Every hour that passes narrows the ground on which hope can still stand,” the MP from Thiruvananthapuram said.
“I am writing to you regarding the Indian nationals who remain missing following the flash floods that struck Nepal on 26 August.
India’s response has been swift and substantial.

The Prime Minister’s early outreach to Kathmandu, the four tranches of relief material, the eleven-member team of doctors, paramedics and tunnel rescue experts, and the control room and Embassy helplines have all made a difference,” Tharoor said.
India’s Ambassador to Nepal Naveem Srivastava and his team have worked round-the-clock, he noted.
“The return of the group from Tibet, whom you personally received at the airport, gave many families their first moment of hope in three days.
The rescue of the Indian workers at Trishuli- 1 was a genuine triumph,” he said.
“Families have noticed all of this.
Several have asked me to convey their gratitude to you personally, and I am glad to do so.

stories.headline: Civic agencies to strengthen flood preparedness at vulnerable locations in Chennai
stories.title: Civic agencies to strengthen flood preparedness at vulnerable locations in Chennai
stories.summary: Out of 207 identified vulnerable locations in GCC, stormwater drains have been constructed in 117 locations
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Civic agencies have started identifying vulnerable locations that are prone to flooding owing to large infrastructure projects including Metrorail, Tangedco and Metrowater in the city.
Owing to intensifying El Niño, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has ordered an allocation of ₹100 crore to execute comprehensive precautionary measures against Northeast Monsoon.
Civic agencies will also implement an action plan for vulnerable locations and provide alternate solutions to prevent flooding this monsoon.

MAWS secretary Gagandeep Singh Bedi conducted a meeting in Ripon Buildings on Saturday with officials of various civic agencies to strengthen monsoon preparedness activities in the city, in the presence of CMRL Managing Director Ashish Chatterjee and Greater Chennai Corporation Commissioner G.S. Sameeran, and senior officials from key stakeholder departments, including WRD, Highways, NHAI, Tangedco, Metrowater, Southern Railway and others.

Out of 207 identified vulnerable locations inside GCC limits, stormwater drains have been constructed in 117 locations, modular storage tanks with high-capacity discharge pumps have been installed in 20 locations, dedicated motor pumps are stationed at 48 locations, and alternate engineering solutions will be implemented for the remaining areas.

The funding of ₹100 crore covers stormwater drain desilting and ward-level relief preparedness, road restoration and repair, procurement and maintenance of heavy-duty motor pumps and deployment of 1,000 seasonal workers for monsoon related works.
A total of 36 GCC boats and 275 fishing boats, arranged via the Fisheries Department, along with trained operators, will be kept on standby.
A total of 215 flood relief centres and 111 community kitchens will be readied.
Desilting is actively under way across 1,671 km of stormwater drains and 1,10,082 silt catch pits throughout the city.
Heavy machinery, motor pumps, and mechanised tree-cutters have been placed on standby.
Over 1,000 general volunteers and 721.
Residents Welfare Association members have been mobilised.

stories.headline: India ready to provide all possible assistance: Rajnath Singh on flash floods in Nepal
stories.title: India ready to provide all possible assistance: Rajnath Singh on flash floods in Nepal
stories.summary: Lucknow , August 29: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday said India was deeply concerned over the devastating flash floods in Nepal and was ready to provide all possible assistance to the neighbouring country. Speaking to reporters in Lucknow, Singh said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had made it clear that India would provide whatever assistance Nepal requires and added that relief support was being sent continuously. "The crisis situation in Nepal is not only worrying the people of Nepal, but India is also concerned about it. The Prime Minister has very clearly stated that whatever assistance is needed, India is ready to provide all of it, and we have started sending assistance continuously," Singh said. According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), the death toll in the Bhote Koshi flood-related disaster in Nepal has reached 626, while 2,426 people are still missing. As per the latest search, rescue and relief update issued by the NDRRMA at 10 am on August 29, Chitwan reported the highest number of deaths, with 233 bodies, including human remains, recovered from the area. Nawalparasi East reported 158 deaths, followed by Nuwakot with 51, Gorkha with 48, Nawalparasi West with 47, Dhading with 45, Tanahun with 31 and Rasua with 13. Other affected areas also reported deaths. The authority said that 2,426 people remained missing. The list includes 27 Nepal Police personnel, 45 Nepal Army personnel, 13 Armed Police Force personnel, 15 Customs Office personnel and four Immigration Office personnel. India has been coordinating relief and rescue efforts in response to the disaster in Nepal, while authorities continue to monitor the situation and the condition of Indian nationals affected by the floods. Nepal President Ramchandra Paudel also expressed gratitude towards India for support and solidarity following a devastating flash flood. Paudel also condoled the demise of Indian nationals in Nepal. (ANI)

stories.headline: 'Water up to 20 feet... climbed trees to stay alive': Indians rescued from flood-hit Nepal
stories.title: 'Water up to 20 feet... climbed trees to stay alive': Indians rescued from flood-hit Nepal
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: After the first batch of 106 stranded Maharashtra tourists reached India, people thanked the Indian and Nepalese authorities for facilitating the rescue.

New Delhi: People from different parts of the country, who were rescued from flood-ravaged Nepal, on Saturday recounted the extent of devastation in the Himalayan Nation and considered themselves lucky to have escaped the catastrophe.
Migrant labourers from Bihar's Bettiah referred to the flash floods as "unimaginable", while speaking to IANS in their hometown.
One of the labourers said, "There were five to seven of us, three of our people went missing...
There was a lot of water in the area, rising up to 20 feet.
We took our children and ran up the hill.
After an hour, when the water level receded, we went to look for them, but we could not find the three people."
"We were told to run away from there as people said there is no guarantee the water (flood) might come again," he added.
A youngster said, "At around 9:30 a.m., I heard a lot of noise.
I went outside to see what was happening, but I could only see dust.
Moments later, I saw that there was a lot of water due to the storm...
Immediately, I alerted the people inside.

stories.headline: Nepal's private, public sectors pledge millions to disaster relief fund
stories.title: Nepal's private, public sectors pledge millions to disaster relief fund
stories.summary: Nepal's public sector, private companies and individuals have pledged millions of rupees to the disaster relief fund as the Himalayan nation continues its fight against one of its worst natural disasters that has killed over 600 people. Nepal is struggling to find its footing after a massive flash flood swept through towns and villages on Wednesday, washing away homes, vehicles, roads and bridges, besides damaging hydropower projects. The death toll crossed 600 on Saturday, while more than 2,400 people remained missing. Nearly 2,500 people, including 163 foreigners, were evacuated as rescue teams raced against time amid intermittent rainfall in flood-affected regions. Nepal's private companies, banks, insurers and individual donors have decided to contribute to the disaster relief fund to help victims, The Kathmandu Post reported. The contributions to the Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund will help authorities treat the injured and provide food and shelter to families displaced
